title: Study plan
description: Discover subjects, structure, exams, teaching approach and much more of the Bachelor in Economics.

blocks.html:
Overview

The Bachelor's degree programme in economics comprises a first common part that focuses on core subjects in the following areas: microeconomics, macroeconomics, finance, business administration, quantitative methods and law.
Subsequently, from the 4th semester onwards, the programme provides four areas of specialisation:

  • Stream in economics
  • Stream in finance
  • Stream in management (with the optional specialisation in Intercultural Communication and Sustainable Economics (ICSE))
  • Stream in quantitative methods

The Bachelor's programme is offered in either Italian (Bachelor in Scienze economiche) or English (Bachelor in Economics)
Each core course is available in both Italian and English. Students may therefore choos to complete all core courses entirely in Italian (Bachelor in Scienze economiche) or entirely in English (Bachelor in Economics).

Study plan

The study plan and course descriptions provide an overview of the programme’s structure and content, and may be subject to changes.
The streams are presented consecutively within the same document.
Enrolled students should refer to the GESTU platform, where they can access the course offering, updated progressively each semester.

items.title: Study plan: additional information
items.html:
ECTS credits distribution

To obtain a Bachelor’s degree in Scienze economiche / Economics, students must earn 180 ECTS, broken down as follows:

  • 19 compulsory core courses: 90 ECTS
  • 8 'stream' first specialisation courses: 48 ECTS
  • 5 elective courses from the other specialisations: 30 ECTS
  • Capstones: 12 ECTS, choosing from the 3 available options:
    • Business game (3 ECTS) + Bachelor Thesis (6 ECTS) + Elective course (3 ECTS)
    • Business game (3 ECTS) + Bachelor Thesis (6 ECTS) + Internship: 3 ECTS
    • Business game (3 ECTS) + Field project (9 ECTS)

Alpine seminar offered by the USI House of Sustainability in Airolo

In accordance with Article 6, paragraph 3 of the Study Regulations, in order to obtain a degree, students are required to complete an alpine seminar offered by the USI House of Sustainability in Airolo. The Alpine seminar is compulsory but does not award any credits.

Elective courses

Among the elective courses in the third academic year, students may take at most one course from another USI Faculty, up to a maximum of 6 ECTS.

The cross-faculty courses ‘Reason and Responsibility in Decision-Making’ (3 ECTS) and ‘Introduction to GenAI: from Theory to Practice’ (3 ECTS) are considered elective courses from another USI faculty and are credited in the third year.

It is recommended that you adhere to the distribution of courses between the second year (4th semester) and the third year (5th and 6th semesters), as well as to the total number of ECTS credits. However, it is possible to:

  • Transfer of ECTS credits obtained from elective courses within the semesters of the same year,
  • Transfer of ECTS credits obtained from elective courses from one academic year to another.

Exception: Specialisation in Management with the ICSE specialisation area, characterised by a defined structure that cannot be modified.

Double specialisation

It is possible to obtain a double specialisation under the following conditions: completion of all courses required for the two specialisations and selection of elective courses from those offered outside the two specialisations.

items.title: Specialisations overview
items.html:
• ​The stream in economics offers a course of study designed to meet the need to analyse and understand both competitive and non-competitive markets. It explores alternative forms of economic organisation that could lead to higher standards of living or a more desirable distribution of wealth.
  • The stream in finance addresses the needs that have arisen in the field of national and international finance. Students study the functioning of financial markets and institutions and learn how to assess, measure and manage the risks associated with financial decisions.
  • The stream in management is designed to provide a solid grounding in the fields of human resource management, production strategies and policies, financial control and marketing for small, medium and large enterprises, both public and private. The area of specialisation in Intercultural Communication and Sustainable Economics (ICSE) features a programme structured for the 6th semester.
  • The stream in quantitative methods offers training in the mathematics and statistics of data science and quantitative analysis in economics.

items.title: Language skills
items.html:
The Bachelor’s programme is offered in Italian (Bachelor in Scienze economiche) or in English (Bachelor in Economics).

Each 'core' courses stream is presented in both Italian and English: students may choose to take the 'core' courses entirely in Italian (Bachelor in Scienze economiche) or entirely in English (Bachelor in Economics).

  • Students who choose the "core" stream in Italian and are not native speakers must present an Italian language certificate of a level of at least B2 from among those recognised by the University within the deadline communicated by the Student Administration.
  • Students who choose the "core" stream in English must present an English language certificate of at least B2 level from among those recognised by the University within the deadlines specified by the Student Administration.

Further information on recognised certificates and the corresponding minimum score requirements is available in the "Application and Admissions" section.
